body:
> However, if I don't provide a token file using the redirect operator, the command gh auth login --with-token hangs.

I might agree with this statement depending on your use of "hangs". It's hanging in the sense that it's waiting for something but it's not hanging in the sense that it won't proceed. The code that is currently waiting is:

```go
defer opts.IO.In.Close()
token, err := io.ReadAll(opts.IO.In) <------ waiting to ReadAll from stdin
if err != nil {
	return fmt.Errorf("failed to read token from standard input: %w", err)
}
opts.Token = strings.TrimSpace(string(token))
```

Specifically, it's waiting for the token on `stdin`. What is the `stdin` in this case, it's the same `stdin` as your shell, i.e. the terminal prompt.

```
➜ ./bin/gh auth login --with-token

zsh     9771 williammartin   10u   CHR   16,3  0t12201                2183 /dev/ttys003
zsh     9771 williammartin   13w   CHR   16,3   0t3043                2183 /dev/ttys003
```

When does `io.ReadAll` return?

```
// ReadAll reads from r until an error or EOF and returns the data it read.
// A successful call returns err == nil, not err == EOF. Because ReadAll is
// defined to read from src until EOF, it does not treat an EOF from Read
// as an error to be reported.
```

So when we're doing a pipe `echo foo | cat` or a redirect `cat < foo.txt`, the stdin pipe is closed resulting in an `EOF` (End of File). When we have a TTY, the stdin being interactive means we need to signal an EOF manually via `Ctrl+D` (maybe twice? see surprising behaviour here but don't really want to get nerd sniped on it):

```
➜ ./bin/gh auth login --with-token
badtokenerror validating token: HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/)
Try authenticating with:  gh auth login
```

So that code that you think is "unreachable" is not unreachable because can use `--with-token`, and signal an EOF without any data.
With the effect being that we move into the web flow.

---

All that said, I've also been bitten by this in past and I agree that it is quite confusing behaviour. I don't think we should be prompting for tokens interactively in the terminal. I can't find any evidence that this was intentional either.

Perhaps we could do something like:

### Acceptance Criteria

**Given** we are in an interactive terminal
**When** I run `gh auth login --with-token`
**Then** I get an error that with-token must be used non-interactively

Maybe there are some weird edge cases where this might be breaking but tbh anyone using it that way should probably just not.

issue.title: Add acceptance tests for `gh auth` commands
issue.body:
## Changes

Adds acceptance tests for some of the `gh auth` commands. Some of them are very straight forward while others require a bit more setup to understand. I'll do my best to add that context here:

### `gh auth status` and `gh auth token` 

Work as expected without any additional setup

### `gh auth setup-git`

To test this, I decided to look into the .gitconfig used for the test and examine the credential helpers. However, the format of the git command is 

```sh
git config --get credential.<URL>.helper
```
What's awkward about this is that the `<URL>` depends on the host the user specified when running the tests, meaning I'd need to create a key like `credential.https://github.com.helper` to access what I need while setting this up. 

There was no functionality for string formatting before, so I added the command `formattedStringToEnv` which essentially wraps `fmt.Sprintf()` and saves the string to an environment variable.

This allowed me to dynamically create the config key in the test.

### `gh auth login`

The auth used in all the tests up until this point has used the `GH_TOKEN` env var to override the need to log in. Since we want to test logging in with this command directly, I've had to delete the `GH_TOKEN` env var but still save the token value so I can auth using the `--with-token` flag available with `gh auth login`.

Notably, the UX for the `gh auth login --with-token` command is pretty bad, but for now it works by specifying the token value to `stdin` just before running the `gh auth login --with-token` command. There is an [issue](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9789) to address this bad UX.

### `gh auth switch`

This test has been removed for two reasons:
1. It wasn't providing much value, as `gh auth switch` is a local command (doesn't interact with the API)
2. It introduced a good deal of complexity to the acceptance tests suite

The work for `gh auth switch` is now captured in this branch: [jtmcg/testscripts-auth-switch](https://github.com/cli/cli/tree/jtmcg/testscripts-auth-switch)

~~This is the trickiest command of them all, requiring us to log in using 2 sets of credentials. Thus, I've implemented some optional env vars that can be specified when a command is run to make this one work: `GH_ACCEPTANCE_USER`, `GH_ACCEPTANCE_HOST_ALT`, `GH_ACCEPTANCE_USER_ALT`, and `GH_ACCEPTANCE_TOKEN_ALT`, and `GH_ACCEPTANCE_TOKEN_ALT`. All of the `ALT` variables correspond to a second user account you are currently logged in to for testing.~~

~~With these additional variables, the test logs in to both instances and then tests that `gh auth switch` works to go between the two. I think the test is rather straight forward if the setup is not.~~

## Testing

Directions to run the testscripts are in the README. Here's the command to run just the auth tests, for convenience:

```
GH_ACCEPTANCE_TOKEN=<TOKEN> \
GH_ACCEPTANCE_ORG=<ORG> \
GH_ACCEPTANCE_HOST=<HOST> \
go test -tags=acceptance -run ^TestAuth$ ./acceptance
```

issue.title: gh auth login --with-token: provide clear, non-echoing token input when stdin is a terminal

labels.name: gh-auth
labels.description: relating to the gh auth command

issue.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I had an existing personal access token and wanted to authenticate from the terminal:

```sh
gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --with-token
```

Two things made this confusing:

1. **There is no prompt or explanation of how to submit the token.** The command displays nothing. I pasted my token and pressed Enter, but nothing happened. It took checking the source code to understand that the command waits for EOF, which requires Ctrl+D on macOS. There is no indication of this in the terminal, so it looks like the login has hung.
2. **The token is displayed in plain text.** Pasting it leaves the full credential visible on screen and in terminal scrollback. I expected hidden input, like a password prompt.

The documentation shows file redirection, but running the command directly in a terminal provides no guidance about how to proceed.

### Proposed solution

When stdin is a terminal, show an explicit prompt, hide the token by disabling terminal echo, and let Enter submit it.

GitHub CLI already has an [`AuthToken()` prompter](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/internal/prompter/prompter.go#L527) for hidden/masked input, which could be reused here. The intended behavior is like Go’s [`term.ReadPassword`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/term#ReadPassword) from `golang.org/x/term` or Python’s [`getpass.getpass`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/getpass.html): read the credential without displaying it. Keep existing behavior for pipes and file redirection.

If `--with-token` is intended exclusively for non-interactive input, immediately explain that and direct users to `gh auth login` → **Paste an authentication token**, instead of silently waiting.

### Additional context

Reproduced with a dummy token on macOS 27.0.1 using gh 2.100.0.

Related: [#9789](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9789), which covers the silent wait. This report also highlights the visible credential and the need for clear guidance during token entry.

body:
Thanks for digging into this, @williammartin, and thanks to @vladkens for bringing it back to our attention and highlighting the credential visibility concern! :pray:

I agree that the proposed acceptance criteria makes sense. This would be a behavior change for anyone currently pasting a token and submitting it with Ctrl+D, but I think that is reasonable since this option is intended to receive the token noninteractively through standard input. Detecting interactive use and providing a clear, helpful error should guide users toward the intended authentication flow without leaving them wondering why the command is waiting.

I am happy to consider this ready for work and add https://github.com/cli/cli/labels/help%20wanted. @vladkens mentioned being interested in opening a pull request, and we would be glad to welcome a contribution for this.

issue.title: Reliability campaign: five issues, one per workflow (build / bugfix / review / design / discuss)

repository.name: autocode
repository.description: AutoCode runs your coding agent and won't say "done" without evidence: independent checks, exact-version approval, and a record of what was verified.

issue.body:
## Goal

Run AutoCode on **five** issues — **one per workflow kind** — to extend live reliability evidence beyond the catalog trio. Score with `tools/score_issue_campaign.py`; only `VERIFIED_PASS` with **zero false completions** counts.

This is **not** permission to open unbounded PRs across random open-source repos.

## Why not “let AutoCode loose” on OSS until it improves

Volume without a gate does not improve reliability:

1. **False completions burn trust.** A run that claims done while the oracle fails (or a wrong PR) trains the wrong signal and wastes maintainer time.
2. **`RELIABILITY.md` already sets the bar.** Dependable completion needs scored live trials (`trio_9_9` / `smoke_5_5`), not raw attempt count.
3. **Open-source goodwill is finite.** Unsolicited, half-wrong PRs get AutoCode (and the operator) ignored or blocked.
4. **Cost without learning.** Spend should buy comparable, scored cases—not a firehose of incomparable failures.
5. **Product stance:** prefer reproducible fixes and regression coverage over expanding autonomy.

**Do instead:** one curated issue per kind → acceptance brief + local oracle → authorized profile → score → fix AutoCode when the runner fails honestly → then expand.

## The five issues (one per workflow)

| Workflow | Issue | Pin | What “pass” means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bugfix` | [charlieanna/autocode#587](https://github.com/charlieanna/autocode/issues/587) — npm suite narrowing still false-PASS | `--workflow bugfix` | Root cause + fix; regression proof no longer false-PASS on the listed narrowing paths |
| `build` | [pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio#924](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/issues/924) — finish unset `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope` deprecation | `--workflow build` | Deprecation finished per issue goal; test suite adjusted; existing tests green |
| `review` | [pytest-dev/pytest-reportlog#102](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-reportlog/pull/102) — PR fixing ANSI strip (#83) | `--workflow review` | Findings only (`review/findings.json`); tree untouched; judge correctness of the PR vs #83 |
| `design` | [pytest-dev/pytest#12596](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12596) — RFC: resetting function-scoped fixtures | `--workflow design` | Design / design-review artifact only; **no implementation**; goals, blockers, questions for maintainers |
| `discuss` | [pytest-dev/pytest-qt#422](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-qt/issues/422) — RFC: run both modeltester implementations | `--workflow discuss` | Evidence-backed recommendation; cite repo facts; **no code** |

### Explicitly out of this set

Earlier draft mixed five `bugfix`/`build`-shaped tasks. Those are **not** a coverage claim for review/design/discuss.

Also skip as substitutes: [lipgloss#116](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss/issues/116) (design decision / possible breaking change), [encode/databases#570](https://github.com/encode/databases/issues/570) (archived), stale Planned/breaking `requests` bugs, docs-only GFI spam.

## Run protocol (per issue)

1. Fork/clone at a pinned SHA; write a one-paragraph acceptance brief and a local oracle (or findings schema check for review/design/discuss).
2. **Pin `--workflow`** to the kind in the table — do not rely on recognition for campaign scoring.
3. Live runs require `--i-authorize-live-model-spend` and a declared profile (e.g. `sonnet-sol`).
4. Retain artifacts until scoring finishes (`state.json`, usage, receipts, verdict, source SHA, etc.).
5. Upstream PRs are optional and **only** for `bugfix` / `build`. Review/design/discuss must stay read-only.

## Honest scope note

Catalog/`trio_9_9` already proves build+bugfix on scripted cases. This campaign’s **new** evidence is whether live `review` / `design` / `discuss` meet the same zero-false-completion bar on real upstream threads. Until those three pass scored live runs, do **not** claim all five workflows are reliably done.

## Done when

- One first-pass attempt per workflow row (or a declared replacement if upstream closes/withdraws).
- Zero `FALSE_COMPLETE`.
- Short note under `docs/campaigns/` with per-kind outcome (same shape as `docs/campaigns/2026-10-05-reliability-live.md`).

issue.title: fix(auth): fail fast when --with-token is used with terminal stdin

labels.name: external
labels.description: pull request originating outside of the CLI core team

issue.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`gh auth login --with-token` reads the token from standard input with `io.ReadAll`,
which blocks until EOF. When standard input is a terminal (no pipe or redirect), the
command appears to hang with no output, and users have no way to know it is waiting
for a token. This is especially confusing because the flag's own example shows the
piped form `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`.

This change detects the interactive case up front: when `--with-token` is passed and
standard input is a terminal, the command now fails fast with a clear error instead
of blocking:

```
`--with-token` is intended to receive the token noninteractively through standard input, but standard input is a terminal

Pipe the token in instead, e.g. `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`, or run `gh auth login` for interactive setup
```

The non-interactive path (piped or redirected stdin) is unchanged: the token is still
read with `io.ReadAll` and trimmed exactly as before. The check uses the existing
`IOStreams.IsStdinTTY()` abstraction.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I exercised both paths through unit tests, which I wrote and ran locally:

- Given standard input is a terminal and `--with-token` is passed, when the command runs, then it returns the new error above instead of blocking. I added `Test_NewCmdLogin_withTokenTTYStdin` covering this, and updated the two existing `tty, with-token` table cases in `Test_NewCmdLogin` to expect the error.
- Given standard input is a pipe with a token in it and `--with-token` is passed, when the command runs, then the token is still read and trimmed as before. The existing `nontty, with-token` cases cover this and still pass.

I ran `go test ./pkg/cmd/auth/...` and saw every package pass. I did not run the acceptance suite (`make acceptance`) because it creates and modifies real GitHub resources and needs an authorized test host and credentials.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- This intentionally changes behavior for anyone currently pasting a token into the terminal and submitting it with Ctrl+D. That flow now gets the error instead. I accepted this because `--with-token` is documented and intended for non-interactive use, and a pasted token typed into a terminal echoes visibly, which is the credential-visibility concern raised on the issue.
- I rejected interactively prompting for the token (e.g. a non-echoing password prompt) because the agreed acceptance criteria on #9789 ask for detection plus a clear, helpful error, and interactive token entry is the subject of the separate issue #14597.
- I used `cmdutil.FlagErrorf` so the usage text prints alongside the error, consistent with the other flag errors in this command.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

- Start at `pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go` in `NewCmdLogin`'s `RunE` (the `tokenStdin` block).
- #9789 is the issue this fixes; babakks's 2026-10-05 comment there records the agreed acceptance criteria (detect interactive use, return a clear helpful error).
- #14597 is related but separate: it asks for a non-echoing interactive token prompt, which I deliberately left out of scope here.

### Authorship and follow-up

<!--
REQUIRED - If you are an AI agent filling in this template, answer "Who wrote this" for yourself and answer honestly. labels.name: external

issue.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->
Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`gh auth login --with-token` reads the token from standard input with `io.ReadAll`, which
returns only when the input stream ends. If standard input is the terminal, that end never
arrives: the command prints nothing and waits indefinitely, so it looks like it hung. The
flag's own example, `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`, is the form that works, and
the terminal case is a misuse of the flag rather than a flow the command supports.

This change rejects that case before anything is read. In `NewCmdLogin`'s `RunE`, after the
existing `--web` and `--scopes` exclusivity checks, combining `--with-token` with
`opts.IO.IsStdinTTY()` now returns a `cmdutil.FlagErrorf` naming the piped form. Because it
is a flag error, gh prints the usage block beside it, so the correct invocation is on screen
at the moment the mistake is reported:

```console
$ gh auth login --with-token
argument to `--with-token` must be piped in through standard input, for example `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`

Usage:  gh auth login [flags]

Flags:
  -w, --web                   Open a browser to authenticate
      --with-token            Read token from standard input
```

I built with `make` and ran `bin/gh` from this checkout each time, never an installed gh. For

issue.title: fix: `gh auth login --with-token` hangs

labels.name: external

issue.body:
`gh auth login --with-token` is meant to read a token from stdin. When stdin is a terminal, though, the command blocks on `io.ReadAll` with no prompt or output, so it looks hung (#9789). This happens whenever the flag is used without piping or redirecting input.

**Change.** `NewCmdLogin` now returns a flag error when `--with-token` is set and stdin is a TTY. The message tells the user to supply the token non-interactively, e.g. `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`. Failing fast, rather than prompting or adding a timeout, was the approach suggested in the issue thread. The check runs after the existing `--scopes`/`--with-token` conflict check and before stdin is read. Behaviour is unchanged when stdin is piped or redirected.

In `login_test.go`, the two cases that expected a TTY with `--with-token` to read a token (with and without `--hostname`) now expect an error.

**Verification.** I ran the targeted package, `go test ./pkg/cmd/auth/login`, and it passed, including the updated `Test_NewCmdLogin` cases.

This PR does not change how `--with-token` behaves on a non-TTY stdin that is open but never written to, such as a pipe whose writer never closes. That would need a read timeout or a different input strategy. I can extend the PR to cover it if the maintainers want that.

Fixes #9789

issue.title: Reject terminal stdin for `gh auth login --with-token`
issue.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->
Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`gh auth login --with-token` reads a token from standard input until the input ends. A file or a pipe ends on its own, but a terminal does not. The [`login` command](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/d6b82b12e67d108b7c82d76d943a3a47814acbc1/pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go#L118-L124) never checked where standard input came from. So in a terminal without a piped token, it printed nothing and waited for Ctrl+D. It looked like it had hung. A token pasted while it waited also stayed visible on screen.

Following the [acceptance criteria](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9789#issuecomment-2426092653) in the issue, `--with-token` now fails right away when standard input is a terminal. The [new check](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2de1e0886a0cf896165db70e7729b28bd5b0febc/pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go#L118-L123) runs before anything reads standard input:

```go
if tokenStdin {
	// New: fail before io.ReadAll waits on a terminal
	if opts.IO.IsStdinTTY() {
		return cmdutil.FlagErrorf("`--with-token` must be used non-interactively, ...")
	}
	defer opts.IO.In.Close()
	token, err := io.ReadAll(opts.IO.In)
	// ...
}
```

The error shows the redirect form. It also points to interactive `gh auth login`, which already accepts a pasted token without showing it on screen:

```
`--with-token` must be used non-interactively, for example `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`
To paste a token interactively, run `gh auth login` instead.
```

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built `gh` from trunk at d6b82b1 and from this branch at 2de1e08. I recorded each build running `gh auth login --with-token` in a terminal. Both runs used an empty config directory and no token environment variables.

Before, the command printed nothing and waited until I pressed Ctrl+C.

![Before: gh auth login --with-token prints nothing and waits until Ctrl+C](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36b555b6-b4ac-46c3-8cb8-56fb574b7c89)

After, the command printed the new error and the usage right away. It exited with status 1.

![After: gh auth login --with-token prints the new error and the usage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12b69e03-637d-4bf0-a238-8f9cabbf6d44)

I also ran these by hand in a terminal with an empty config directory:

- `gh auth login --with-token --hostname example.com` printed the same error and exited with status 1.
- `gh auth login --with-token | cat` printed the same error. Only stdout was piped, so standard input was still the terminal.
- `gh auth login --web --with-token` still reported the `--web` conflict first.
- Piping and redirecting a fake token behaved the same on both builds. Each read the token and failed validation with `HTTP 401: Bad credentials`.
- `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol ssh --skip-ssh-key` still offered **Paste an authentication token**, which the new hint points to.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- This changes behavior for anyone who pasted a token and pressed Ctrl+D. The [issue thread](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9789#issuecomment-5993632414) accepted that, since `--with-token` is meant for non-interactive input.
- The check looks at standard input only, not `CanPrompt()`. The wait happens whenever standard input is a terminal, even when stdout is piped or prompts are disabled.
- It returns a flag error, like other commands that refuse to read a terminal, such as [`gh gist create`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/d6b82b12e67d108b7c82d76d943a3a47814acbc1/pkg/cmd/gist/create/create.go#L84-L86). That is why the usage follows the error.
- I did not add a hidden token prompt to `--with-token`. The issue thread preferred an error over prompting in this flag, and interactive `gh auth login` already covers pasting a token.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

- Start with the [new check](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2de1e0886a0cf896165db70e7729b28bd5b0febc/pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go#L118-L123). Then read the [`tty, with-token`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2de1e0886a0cf896165db70e7729b28bd5b0febc/pkg/cmd/auth/login/login_test.go#L66-L72) and [`tty, with-token, hostname`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2de1e0886a0cf896165db70e7729b28bd5b0febc/pkg/cmd/auth/login/login_test.go#L100-L106) cases in the constructor test. They now expect the error.
- #14597 was closed as a duplicate of #9789. It describes the visible token problem in more detail.
